text: VN-Index falls below 1,700-point threshold

HÀ NỘI - The market extended its losing streak on Thursday, with broad-based selling pressure dragging the VN-Index below the psychologically important 1,700-point threshold for the first time in the recent three-session decline.
The benchmark, representing the Hochiminh Stock Exchange (HoSE), fell 13.39 points to close at 1,689.62 points.
After three consecutive sessions of losses, the index had shed a total of 47.27 points.
Market breadth remained firmly negative, with 207 stocks declining, compared with 107 gainers.
Trading value on the HoSE fell nearly 14 per cent from the previous trade to VNĐ15 trillion (US$583 million).
The VN30-Index, which tracks the 30 largest stocks by market capitalisation and liquidity, dropped 18.03 points to 1,788.51 points.
Twenty-one of its 30 constituents closed lower, five were unchanged and four advanced.
FPT Corporation (FPT) recorded the steepest decline in the VN30 basket, falling 2.66 per cent.
LPBank (LPB) followed with a loss of 2.29 per cent, while Vingroup (VIC) dropped 2.04 per cent.
VIC remained the biggest drag on the VN-Index, shaving nearly eight points off the benchmark.
CTG reduced the index by 0.8 points, followed by VHM with a negative contribution of 0.69 points.
Banking stocks continued to face selling pressure, with several large-cap lenders closing lower.
Sacombank (STB) lost 1.71 per cent and Asia Commercial Joint Stock Bank (ACB) declined 0.99 per cent.
Techcombank (TCB) dropped 0.72 per cent, MBBank (MBB) slipped 0.53 per cent and HDBank (HDB) fell 0.45 per cent.
LPB extended its decline for a third consecutive session, falling 2.29 per cent to VNĐ34,200 per share.
Compared with its closing price at the beginning of the week, the stock had lost nearly 8 per cent.
VIB and BIDV (BID) were among the few banking stocks to post gains, rising 0.37 per cent and 0.49 per cent, respectively.
On the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX), the HNX-Index also closed lower, shedding 3.79 points to 238.94 points.
This marked its fifth straight day of declining.
Investors poured over VNĐ645 billion into the northern bourse, equal to a trading volume of nearly 53.6 million shares.
Foreign investors continued to add to market pressure, recording net sales of more than VNĐ1 trillion across the market.
FPT faced the heaviest foreign net selling, at VNĐ272.1 billion, while ACB followed with VNĐ101.5 billion in net sales. - BIZHUB/VNS
